Transcript body:
00:00 Marcus: hey everyone, thanks for joining. good to see you all. um quick check — are we all on video?
00:08 Priya: yeah we're here, sorry i was in another meeting.
00:11 Marcus: no worries. today's goal is short — go over the observed spikes from the canary yesterday, confirm next steps for the kernel upgrade and the rollback if anything regresses, and then schedule a dry run for hosted fallback.
00:28 Samir: sounds good. we saw two notable tails yesterday, one around 13:04 UTC and another ~13:42. the 99th jumped from ~220ms to 1.1s for a few minutes.
00:40 Ivy: mmm-hmm. do you still have the perf logs? can you pull the per-route breakdown? we suspect egress shaping, but it could be route flaps between the customer VPC and the private nodes.
00:53 Samir: yes, i pulled the logs. i'm attaching the perf log later, but quick note, it correlates with our egress batching spike — could be bufferbloat or queuing in their edge.
01:05 Daniel: also fwiw, we saw a few TCP retransmits coincident with that time window. so there's definite packet loss, small but impactful for tail latency.
01:18 Olivia: from security side, we didn't see any auth failures. certs are fine. KMS calls were fine but we need to confirm if the KMS endpoint IPs are whitelisted for the private deployment.
01:30 Marcus: ok good. on the kernel side, the plan is to roll kernel 5.15.3 -> 5.15.5 with our optimized attention kernels turned on for the quantized variant. it's a targeted change to the memory allocator and the fused attention path. Ivy, correct me if i'm misstating.
01:47 Ivy: yeah that's right. the change touches the allocator and the new optimized fused GEMM kernels. we saw some different latency distributions in staging — normally the mean is stable but the 99th can get worse if there's unexpected contention in the allocator.
02:03 Priya: small question — could the quantized model path be amplifying the tail? we did see slightly different KV cache behavior when we enabled 4-bit quant.
02:15 Ivy: that's possible, especially with the prefix cache and frequent small prompt bursts. quantization reduces compute but can shift memory access patterns. we should capture KV cache hit rates and correlate with per-token latencies.
02:28 Marcus: agreed. so action item: Ivy to run a deterministic workload and export per-token histograms and KV cache hits.
02:36 Ivy: yep i'll run the benchmark tomorrow morning and share CSV. i'll include warm and cold cache runs.
02:42 Samir: about the network — we did a trace and see a couple of micro-flaps in the BGP session between the peering. it looks like route updates coincided with the spike windows. might be our edge provider TTL settings.
02:56 Marcus: okay so we have two hypotheses: network micro-flaps causing retransmits and kernel allocator contention with quant path. we should tackle both in parallel.
03:08 Priya: agreed. what about fallback? last time we did a manual fallback to hosted model and it masked the issue but we want a more deterministic dry-run.
03:19 Lena: i'll own the hosted dry-run scheduling. propose Tuesday 2026-03-23 09:00 PT for a 30-minute window where we simulate surge and failover to hosted.
03:31 Marcus: perfect. Samir will you be able to provide packet captures during that window so we can compare?
03:36 Samir: yes, i'll schedule the capture. we'll do tcptrace and iperf during the dry-run.
03:43 Olivia: and i'll validate KMS whitelisting before then. want to ensure keys are accessible when we hit hosted fallback.
03:51 Daniel: quick note — if we enable the new kernel image, what's the rollback path? we need an automated canary rollback that won't leave us in a bad state.
04:02 Marcus: good point. the plan is: staged canary -> monitor key metrics (p95/p99, error rate) -> if regression exceeds threshold for 5 minutes, automatic rollback to previous image and route traffic back. i'll send the exact thresholds in the doc.
04:18 Priya: can you put the thresholds in the ticket so engineering can sign off?
04:22 Marcus: yep i'll include p95/p99 thresholds and SLOs.
04:25 Ivy: and i'll add the benchmark CSV so you can see the distribution.
04:30 Samir: one more network data point — during the earlier incident we saw queuing in the customer egress that created bursts of 30-40ms per-packet; aggregated for multi-token requests that's compounding to the 1s tail.
04:44 Marcus: hmm ok. that suggests we also need to tune our batching/worker timeouts and maybe reduce the maximum batch wait for this pilot. ivv? ivY? (fumbling)
04:54 Ivy: yes — lowering batch wait to 10ms for the pilot with smaller batch sizes could help. but it will increase cpu and possibly token cost. tradeoff.
05:05 Priya: cost is okay for the pilot; our priority is stable latency. we'll accept a little extra cost for determinism.
05:12 Olivia: on compliance, do we need changes to audit logs if we toggle to hosted fallback?
05:18 Lena: the hosted fallback will still log session provenance; we'll ensure mapping back to tenant IDs. olivia, we'll share the audit mapping doc after the call.
05:27 Olivia: great. also confirm whether we need HSM-level access or if managed KMS is ok for the pilot.
05:33 Marcus: note - olivia will confirm.
05:35 Daniel: for the kernel image build, what's the image tag naming convention? we want immutable tags to make rollback safe.
05:41 Ivy: we publish tags like redwood-infer:5.15.5-20260312-optim1; rollback will be to redwood-infer:5.15.3-20260225. we'll put those exact tags in the playbook.
05:55 Samir: i'll need the playbook to coordinate SRE steps, esp. draining nodes and cache warming.
06:02 Marcus: ok i'll share the playbook after this call. also include the canary traffic percentages and thresholds.
06:08 Priya: question - do we have a way to force KV cache eviction for deterministic cold runs?
06:14 Ivy: yes we have an admin endpoint to flush prefix cache; i'll include instructions.
06:19 Marcus: perfect. any blockers from meridian's side?
06:22 Samir: main blocker is getting packet captures during our maintenance window; after that we can correlate. also need to confirm egress provider TTL settings — we'll follow up.
06:33 Olivia: and from security, need confirmation that the KMS endpoints are open. that's on me.
06:37 Marcus: great. recap: Marcus will send playbook and thresholds, Ivy will run benchmark and share CSV, Samir will provide traces, Olivia confirms KMS, Lena schedules hosted dry-run.
06:52 Priya: sounds good. thanks all.
06:55 Marcus: thanks everyone — we'll regroup next week same time unless we need an ad-hoc. bye.
07:00 [call ends]
